page: Vultr vx1-g-48c-192g is a general-purpose cloud server instance belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical AMD EPYC cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2.0 threads per core. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz and is supported by 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance includes a minimal 1 GB network-attached local storage volume and does not feature any GPU accelerators.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong compute and memory capabilities. Single-core performance is highly competitive, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 10% tier. Multi-core performance is also robust, ranking in the top 25% for stress-ng and the top 10% for Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory subsystem performance is a highlight, with uncached large-block read and write bandwidth both achieving top 10% tier results. The CPU support for advanced vector extensions and cryptographic acceleration contributes to strong performance in specialized tasks, such as database operations and text processing, which both rank in the top 10% tier.

A notable architectural tradeoff is the storage configuration; with only 1 GB of network-based local storage, workloads requiring high-capacity or high-throughput local disk I/O must rely on external network storage volumes. However, the high memory capacity and dedicated CPU allocation make this instance highly cost-efficient for resource-dense, compute-heavy deployments that do not require local storage. The system is well-suited for workloads such as large-scale database operations, software compilation, static web serving, and CPU-based LLM text generation, where it maintains top-tier token generation speeds even for larger models.
